summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported, from a backer back from England, that Allen had sparred George Rooke around the country, forfeited a crooked match with him, and was matched with Gilbert, but hoped to return to America.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Sunday Morning, October 7, 1877

facts.fact: In 1877 Allen and George Rooke gave sparring exhibitions throughout England; Allen's first exhibition in his home town of Birmingham drew the largest crowd for such an affair in eighteen years
Sparring with gloves at Manchester, Allen knocked George Rooke out of time
Rooke's Birmingham friends matched him against Allen with £25 forfeit a side; Allen forfeited after concluding the 'gang' was with Rooke and the fight would not be decided on its merits
Allen was matched to box Gilbert in a 24-foot ring under the new London rules for £50 a side on October 29, 1877
Allen wished to return to America and thought that, since Joe Goss had been freed, his trouble in Kentucky might blow over, when he would recross the Atlantic

notes: Secondhand account from an unnamed friend and backer of Allen just back from two months in England. Relates to existing note that Allen waited out his Kentucky legal trouble.
